# Watch damage from ASSS 1.4.4 src/core/watchdamage.c (compiled unmodified).
#   seat <pairs>   one pair per player: 'c' a Continuum client or 'v' a VIE client,
#      then 'p' playing in this arena, 'o' in another arena, 'n' with no arena
#   cmd <player> player <target> [<args>]   ran ?watchdamage aimed at one player
#   cmd <player> arena [<args>]             ran it as a public command
#   modwatch <player> <0|1>  called Iwatchdamage::ModuleWatch, which is how another
#      module asks for a player's damage without being a watcher itself
#   leave <player>   ran the PA_LEAVEARENA player action
#   damage <player> count=<n> tick=<n> fill=<byte> len=<n>   fed the module a
#      C2S 0x32 of that length carrying that many damage records
#   pkt set|one [<player>] <hex>   each packet, in order and in wire order.
#      'set' is a send to the watcher list, 'one' names a single recipient.
#   cb <name>      each callback fired
#   chat <player> <text>   each chat line and who got it
#   state <player>:<watchers>/<modwatch>/<watcher list>...   per player: how many
#      others are watching THEIR damage, the module-watch counter on them, and
#      which players those watchers are.
#
# Rules these records pin:
#
# 1. The watch count that decides whether the client is toggled is
#    LLCount(watches) + modwatch, and the S2C 0x37 toggle is sent ONLY when a watch
#    is added and the total becomes exactly 1, or removed and it becomes 0.
# 2. ModuleWatch NEVER SENDS A PACKET. It only moves the counter. So a module that
#    asks for a player's damage while nobody else is watching bumps the total from
#    0 to 1 with no toggle going out, and the client is never told to start
#    reporting -- and because the total is then already 1, the first real watcher
#    to come along takes it to 2 and does not send one either. The module's damage
#    callback then never fires. Records below drive exactly that order.
# 3. The decrement is floored: ModuleWatch(off) on a player whose counter is
#    already 0 leaves it at 0 rather than going negative.
# 4. The toggle is sent only to T_CONT players. A VIE client is added to the watch
#    list and counted like anyone else, but never receives the toggle, so it never
#    reports -- and ?watchdamage aimed AT a non-Continuum player is refused outright
#    with a message naming them.
# 5. ?watchdamage with exactly '0' or '1' forces that state; anything else, the
#    empty string included, TOGGLES -- and the toggle is implemented by trying to
#    add and removing again if the add reported it was already there.
# 6. The public form only does anything for exactly '0', which clears all of that
#    player's watches on others. Any other argument, '1' included, is silently
#    ignored.
# 7. ClearWatch on leaving the arena is called with himtoo=1, so it removes both
#    his watches on other people AND the list of people watching him. Removing his
#    own watches goes through RemoveWatch, so the people he was watching get their
#    toggle-off packets; emptying his own watcher list does NOT, so HE is never
#    told to stop -- he is leaving anyway.
# 8. The damage packet's length must satisfy (len - 5) % sizeof(DamageData) == 0,
#    and the relayed S2C 0x38 is 7 bytes of header plus the records copied
#    verbatim. The server fills in the damaged player's id, which the C2S does not
#    carry. A report with zero records is valid and is relayed as a bare header.
# 9. The relay goes out before the callback, and the callback fires only when
#    modwatch is above zero -- the comment in the source says these can go in mass
#    spamming, so it is deliberate.
sizes DamageData=9 C2SWatchDamage_header=5 S2C_header=7
seat cpcpcp
state 0:0/0/- 1:0/0/- 2:0/0/-
cmd 0 player 1 []
state 0:0/0/- 1:1/0/0 2:0/0/-
pkt one 1 3701
chat 0 Damage watching on p1 turned on
cmd 0 player 1 []
state 0:0/0/- 1:0/0/- 2:0/0/-
pkt one 1 3700
chat 0 Damage watching on p1 turned off

state 0:0/0/- 1:1/0/0 2:0/0/-
pkt one 1 3701
chat 0 Damage watching on p1 turned on
cmd 0 player 1 [1]
state 0:0/0/- 1:1/0/0 2:0/0/-
chat 0 Damage watching on p1 turned on
cmd 2 player 1 [1]
state 0:0/0/- 1:2/0/02 2:0/0/-
chat 2 Damage watching on p1 turned on
cmd 0 player 1 [0]
state 0:0/0/- 1:1/0/2 2:0/0/-
chat 0 Damage watching on p1 turned off
cmd 2 player 1 [0]
state 0:0/0/- 1:0/0/- 2:0/0/-
pkt one 1 3700
chat 2 Damage watching on p1 turned off
cmd 0 player 1 [0]
state 0:0/0/- 1:0/0/- 2:0/0/-

state 0:0/0/- 1:1/0/0 2:0/0/-

chat 1 Damage watching on p0 turned on
# p0 leaves: p1 and p2 get toggle-offs, p0's own watcher list is just
# emptied, so p0 is never told to stop
leave 0
state 0:0/0/- 1:0/0/- 2:0/0/-

pkt one 2 3700
